title: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine
description_short: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine
description_medium: The timeline dates Semion Mogilevich’s birth in Kyiv to June 30, 1946. A 2014 Business Insider profile also places his birth in Kyiv that year and later describes him as a Russian organized-crime figure, summarizing FBI allegations involving fraud and other transnational crime. The supplied accounts do not establish a connection to Donald Trump.
description_long: The timeline records Semion Mogilevich’s birth in Kyiv on June 30, 1946. A 2014 Business Insider profile supports the year and city, then describes Mogilevich as an organized-crime figure and summarizes allegations attributed to U.S. authorities. The article says the FBI named him among its most wanted fugitives and recounts an alleged investor-fraud scheme involving YBM Magnex, a Canadian company. It also describes a 1998 FBI report about an organization attributed to Mogilevich and alleged activity that included money laundering and trafficking. The profile reports that Mogilevich denied wrongdoing in a BBC interview, saying authorities would have to prove their claims. Those later allegations provide biographical context, but they are not findings about the birth event itself. The supplied material does not establish why Mogilevich appears in this Trump-related timeline or show a connection between him and Donald Trump. The timeline page was inaccessible in a focused read, and the linked profile confirms the birth year and city but not June 30 specifically.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Semion Mogilevich, the ‘boss of bosses,' is born in Ukraine

notes: Needs context: the supplied materials do not explain Mogilevich’s inclusion in this Trump-related timeline or establish any Trump connection; the focused TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202. The exact June 30 birthday is not independently confirmed by the linked profile, which confirms only year and city.
Proposed correction: retain the biography only if the exact date is verified, and add a sourced explanation of the Trump connection or remove the record from the Trump timeline.

title: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
description_short: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
description_medium: Jeffrey Epstein began teaching mathematics and physics at New York’s Dalton School in September 1974, after headmaster Donald Barr announced he would leave at the school year’s end. Later accounts from former students described concerning behavior and said some raised concerns with an administrator. The available reporting does not identify who hired Epstein or show what school officials knew then.
description_long: Jeffrey Epstein joined the faculty of New York’s Dalton School in September 1974, teaching mathematics and physics. Donald Barr, the school’s headmaster and father of future attorney general William Barr, had announced that he would leave at the end of that school year. The New York Times later reported former students’ recollections that Epstein crossed boundaries in his interactions with girls and that some students raised concerns with an administrator. Those recollections concern Epstein’s conduct at school; the supplied account does not place the conversations at the time of hiring. The linked reporting could not be opened in a focused read, and the current draft likewise does not identify who selected Epstein for the job, describe the hiring process, or establish that Donald Barr knew of misconduct when Epstein joined the faculty. The timeline’s headline therefore makes a specific claim that its available supporting account does not substantiate. The defensible chronology is that Epstein started teaching while Barr was headmaster and Barr was preparing to leave; that sequence alone does not establish that Barr personally hired him.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School

notes: Needs context: the linked New York Times article returned HTTP 403; the supplied draft describes Epstein’s start and later student accounts but does not identify his hirer or establish Donald Barr’s role in the appointment.
Proposed correction: change the headline to say Epstein joined the Dalton faculty while Donald Barr was headmaster unless a source identifies Barr as the person who hired him.

title: Trump: Tony Schwartz publishes negative Trump story, Trump hires him
description_short: Trump: Tony Schwartz publishes negative Trump story, Trump hires him
description_medium: In 1985, Tony Schwartz published a critical New York magazine profile of Donald Trump, who nevertheless praised the piece and sent Schwartz a fan note. Later that year, Trump offered Schwartz half the advance and royalties to ghostwrite The Art of the Deal. Schwartz accepted, and the book project began a close working relationship that lasted eighteen months.
description_long: Tony Schwartz’s 1985 New York magazine story presented Donald Trump as a struggling landlord rather than the triumphant developer celebrated in his public image. Schwartz described Trump’s unsuccessful effort to remove rent-controlled tenants from a building on Central Park South, including a plan to place homeless people in the building to pressure residents. The magazine’s cover showed Trump sweaty and unshaven. The New Yorker later reported that Trump liked the critical story, displayed its cover in his office and sent Schwartz a complimentary note. The two met again when Schwartz interviewed Trump for Playboy. Trump said he had signed a book deal and needed to save material for the project; Schwartz suggested the title The Art of the Deal. After considering the offer for several weeks, Schwartz agreed to ghostwrite the book in exchange for half the advance and half the royalties. Trump accepted those terms. Beginning in late 1985, Schwartz spent eighteen months working closely with Trump, including time at his office, meetings and homes. The resulting 1987 book carried both men’s names and became a bestseller. The episode connects a critical profile to the later collaboration that helped shape Trump’s public image.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Tony Schwartz publishes negative Trump story, Trump hires him
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Tony Schwartz publishes negative Trump story, Trump hires him

notes: The New Yorker says Schwartz later accepted Trump’s offer to split the advance and royalties; it also recounts that the book project was first developed by publisher Si Newhouse and Random House.

title: Trump: Robert Maxwell obtains passports for Mogilevich, helps KGB
description_short: Trump: Robert Maxwell obtains passports for Mogilevich, helps KGB
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline alleges that Robert Maxwell arranged Israeli passports for Semion Mogilevich and 23 associates in 1988, then connects the group to a Bank of New York account it says was used for laundering. Its TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202 in a focused read, and the supplied record provides no independent documentation for the passport or KGB claims.
description_long: The supplied timeline attributes two serious claims to Robert Maxwell: that he obtained Israeli passports for Semion Mogilevich and 23 associates in 1988, and that he connected Mogilevich to a Bank of New York account used to launder money. It further says the passports and account helped Mogilevich expand a criminal network and titles the event as Maxwell helping the KGB. The record does not include passport records, bank documents, court findings or contemporaneous reporting that independently confirms those assertions. Its current draft describes the TrumpFile page’s references as secondary material, including a book, rather than direct evidence of the alleged transactions. The page itself returned HTTP 202 during a focused read, so its full wording and citations could not be checked here. Because the passport, banking and intelligence claims are the substance of the event, they should remain attributed allegations rather than statements of established fact. The supplied material also does not explain how this 1988 account relates to Donald Trump. A reliable account needs independent reporting or primary records that establish what Maxwell did, when it happened and whether the alleged KGB connection is supported.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Robert Maxwell obtains passports for Mogilevich, helps KGB
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Robert Maxwell obtains passports for Mogilevich, helps KGB

notes: Needs context: the linked timeline returned HTTP 202, and supplied citations do not independently verify the passport transfer, bank account, alleged laundering or KGB assistance; the record also gives no Trump connection.
Proposed correction: present these as attributed allegations only if independent documentation supports them, and omit the KGB claim unless a source substantiates it.

title: Donald Trump sues the U.S. government for discrimination
description_short: Donald Trump sues the U.S. government for discrimination
description_medium: In 1993, Donald Trump sued the federal government over the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act, arguing that the law favored tribal casinos and disadvantaged casino owners such as himself. The supplied account says he also challenged the law on states’ rights grounds and sought to block tribal casinos. It does not provide the court’s decision or the case’s later procedural history.
description_long: Donald Trump filed a federal lawsuit in 1993 challenging the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act, the 1988 law governing tribal gaming. As summarized in the supplied account, Trump argued that the law discriminated against him as a casino owner by allowing Native American tribes to open casinos, and he also claimed it infringed states’ rights. The New York Times headline linked to the record says the suit sought to block Indian casinos. These are arguments attributed to Trump’s complaint, not a judicial finding that the statute discriminated against him or violated states’ rights. The record does not identify the specific tribal parties, lay out the complete legal arguments, or show how the court resolved the dispute. Its linked Times report returned HTTP 403 in a focused read, and the supplied draft contained no ruling or docket details. The filing can be described as a challenge to tribal gaming under federal law, but the outcome and the court’s reasoning remain unknown from the available material. A fuller account needs the complaint or docket and a reliable source on the procedural disposition before it can say whether the suit was dismissed, decided on the merits or otherwise concluded.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump sues the U.S. government for discrimination
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump sues the U.S. government for discrimination

notes: Needs context: the linked Times article returned HTTP 403; supplied notes give a limited summary of the complaint but no docket, full party list, or procedural outcome.
Proposed correction: describe the discrimination and states’ rights theories as Trump’s claims, and add the case disposition only after checking the docket or an accessible report.
